To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

three novel pathogenic mutations of the K _{ATP} channel genes and somatically altered imprinting patterns of the 11 p15 region in pancreatic tissues were detected in patients with congenial hyperinsulinism.
we identified 4 novel ABCC8 or KATP mutations, and we showed that the 11p imprinting alteration is a central event in focal CHI
we found three novel ABCC8 and one novel KCNJ11 gene mutations in patients with congenial hyperinsulinism, and we identified epigenetic alterations at 11p 15 region in patients with CHI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular etiology and pathology of CHI.
the molecular pathology of focal and diffuse CHI and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of CHI.
the identification of novel pathogenic mutations and somatic imprint alterations of the 1p15 region in patients with CHI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

focal CHI is caused by paternally inherited KATP channel mutations and maternal allelic losses at the 11 p15 region, and that diffuse CHI is caused either by paternally and maternally inherited K-ATP channel mutations or by a somatic mutation within a normal K-ATP gene.
the molecular pathogenesis of focal CHI is the presence of heterozygous mutations of the K(ATP) channel genes, and the loss of the imprinting of the IGF2 gene in the pancreatic lesion.
focal and diffuse CHI are caused by distinct pathogenic mechanisms, i.e. somatic imprinting alteration and somatic mutation, respectively, of the 11 p15 region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
focal and diffuse forms of CHI are distinct disorders, and that the focal form is a result of somatic mutation of the KATPP channel genes and somatically imprinted alteration of the 11 p15 region.
the KATP mutation is the cause of CHI, but the epigenetic alteration is necessary for developing the disease.
focal CHI can be caused by paternally inherited KATP channel mutations and somatic imprint loss at the 11 p15 region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified three new genetic mutations in the KATP genes and have also shown that the 11p region is important in the development of CHI.

we have shown that the KATP mutations are present in the focal lesion in patients with congenitally hyperinsulinemic focal adenomatous hyperlasias, which is a finding that has not previously been reported in the literature.
we have found that the molecular etiology in CHI is not limited to mutations in KAT channel subunit genes.
